title: Contribution and Reproducibility of Lung Ultrasound in the Diagnosis of Acute Heart Failure in the ED
brief_summary: Discrimination between cardiac and non-cardiac causes of dyspnea can be challenging, causing excessive delay before adequate therapy. In clinical practice lung ultrasound (LUS) is becoming an easy and reliable noninvasive tool for the evaluation of dyspnea and can shorten the time to diagnosis .However the reproductibility of this test was not extensively studied.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* non traumatic dyspnea with the final diagnosis of heart failure

Exclusion Criteria:

* impossibility to give consent to participate in the study
* post traumatic dyspnea
* pregnant women
* need for endotracheal intubation or inotropic drugs
* patients who were deemed too unstable for sonography by the treating team
study_population: all patients admitted to the ED with acute dyspnea, with the final diagnosis of heart failure
